name: datamade/scrapers-us-municipal
what_it_holds: DataMade's fork/production deployment (1,680 commits, MIT license) of the Legistar-based municipal scraper covering Chicago, Cook County, Ferguson, LA Metro, Miami-Dade, New York City, Pittsburgh, Sacramento, and St. Louis city councils, feeding ocd.datamade.us.
why_useful: Ready-configured scrapers for several cities already in our STR panel (NYC, LA-area via LA Metro, Chicago) to pull the underlying council legislative record (ordinance introduction/vote dates) around STR regulation, useful as a companion to the registry data we already hold.
geography: Chicago, Cook County, Ferguson MO, LA Metro, Miami-Dade, NYC, Pittsburgh, Sacramento, St. Louis
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: Ready-configured scrapers for several cities already in our STR panel (NYC, LA-area via LA Metro, Chicago) to pull the underlying council legislative record (ordinance introduction/vote dates) around STR regulation, useful as a companion to the registry data we already hold.

name: freelawproject/courtlistener
what_it_holds: The full open-source codebase (25,363 commits, AGPL license) behind CourtListener.com, Free Law Project's searchable archive of federal/state court opinions, oral arguments, judges, and (via RECAP) federal docket filings; the live site and its API/bulk-data exports (not directly confirmed in this fetch, but documented at wiki.free.law) can be queried for Airbnb Inc. litigation (e.g. host/guest class actions, city-vs-Airbnb regulatory suits, IP/antitrust cases) with case metadata and filing dates.
why_useful: The best free method to build a point-in-time litigation docket for Airbnb (host lawsuits, city STR-ordinance enforcement suits, DOJ/FTC matters) that could carry event-study/regulatory-risk signal for gap #12 and the events/shocks gap (#11); the codebase itself is not a dataset but confirms the underlying API/bulk data exist to query.
time_coverage: federal courts back to ~1600s for some opinions per site; RECAP dockets from ~2009-present
size_hint: 9M+ opinions per topic-page description; codebase itself large (25k+ commits)
last_activity: actively maintained (937 open issues, ongoing commits)
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: The best free method to build a point-in-time litigation docket for Airbnb (host lawsuits, city STR-ordinance enforcement suits, DOJ/FTC matters) that could carry event-study/regulatory-risk signal for gap #12 and the events/shocks gap (#11); the codebase itself is not a dataset but confirms the underlying API/bulk data exist to query.

name: CouncilDataProject (org: cdp-backend, cdp-scrapers, speakerbox, and per-city repos)
what_it_holds: A 'search engine for local government' spanning 18+ US municipalities (Seattle, Denver, Oakland, Charlotte, Milwaukee, Boston, Pittsburgh, Atlanta, others), combining city-council meeting video/audio transcription (speakerbox), a scraping pipeline (cdp-scrapers), and a searchable backend (cdp-backend, MPL-2.0) that stores meeting minutes, agenda items, and vote records per city, each in its own per-city GitHub/cloud-hosted deployment.
why_useful: Deeper than plain Legistar scraping: full-text-searchable council meeting transcripts could surface STR-ordinance debates, votes, and public comment in cities we already track (Seattle, Boston, Pittsburgh) or add new ones, feeding gap #12 with qualitative/timestamped regulatory-process detail rather than just bill metadata.
geography: 18+ US cities (Seattle, Denver, Oakland, Charlotte, Milwaukee, Boston, Pittsburgh, Atlanta, others)
size_hint: distributed across per-city cloud-hosted databases + GitHub org repos; not a single flat file
last_activity: not confirmed, org appears active with multiple maintained sub-repos
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: Deeper than plain Legistar scraping: full-text-searchable council meeting transcripts could surface STR-ordinance debates, votes, and public comment in cities we already track (Seattle, Boston, Pittsburgh) or add new ones, feeding gap #12 with qualitative/timestamped regulatory-process detail rather than just bill metadata.

name: BailleurVerif - French Non-Compliant Rental Listings Observatory
what_it_holds: Time-stamped, longitudinal dataset on data.gouv.fr (French government open-data portal) tracking short-term rental listings in France found non-compliant with local registration/regulation rules (an 'observatory' feed maintained by BailleurVerif). Cataloged in awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets under Government (BailleurVerif.yml).
why_useful: Directly on-point for gap 12 (STR ordinance trackers / city registration datasets) for France, which the CONTEXT gap list names as a target geography (France STR registration) but we don't yet hold a France-specific compliance/registration series; a longitudinal non-compliance count could proxy enforcement intensity and registered-listing counts over time.
time_coverage: ongoing, dated snapshots (exact start unclear from listing)
size_hint: unknown row count; time-stamped longitudinal series
license: French open-data licence (Licence Ouverte, per data.gouv.fr defaults)

name: numbeopy
what_it_holds: Python client (rate-limited, dependency-light) that pulls Numbeo's public cost-of-living pages via pandas.read_html: country-aggregate prices, per-city indices (50-70 price items per country incl. rent, restaurants, utilities, salaries), and country-level indices (6 cost-of-living sub-indices) plus category rankings (quality of life, property investment, crime, health care, pollution, traffic). No data committed; live pull only. CC BY-NC 4.0 license (non-commercial, attribution required, bulk redistribution discouraged). Last activity ~Jul 2026.
why_useful: Numbeo's cost-of-living and rent indices per city are a live, low-cost way to track relative travel/rent affordability across ABNB's top international markets, which could feed a cross-market affordability adjustment for ADR/nights forecasts.
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (Numbeo data terms, per repo description)
themes: Currency and travel affordability crowdsourced data: Numbeo, Expatistan, hotel price indices (Hotels.com HPI archives), Trivago Hotel Price Index, Kayak price trackers
why_all: Numbeo's cost-of-living and rent indices per city are a live, low-cost way to track relative travel/rent affordability across ABNB's top international markets, which could feed a cross-market affordability adjustment for ADR/nights forecasts.

Cleanest available Numbeo client for a repeatable, dateable pull of a global affordability/cost-of-living index across many cities - could be stamped and reused as a point-in-time consumer-affordability proxy (ties to gap #6, consumer spend panels) with minimal engineering; no committed history exists yet so it would need to be run and vintage-stamped by the team.
